result:
The proposed answer is correct: the limit is (1−λ)/log(1/λ). I checked each step of the argument.

**Structure.** The tree is a spine (i,0) with a path of length i attached at each (i,0). Since λ<1, the walk is biased away from the root, so on the spine it drifts outward and inside each finger it drifts toward the leaf. Cut times can only occur at first crossings of spine edges, because the walk must return to the base of any finger it enters.

**Spine walk.** From a spine vertex, the weights are λ for the parent, 1 for the next spine vertex and 1 for the finger. Excursions into a finger return to the same vertex, so the induced spine walk steps right with probability 1/(1+λ) and left with probability λ/(1+λ). A time k is a cut time exactly when the spine edge e_i=(i,0)–(i+1,0) is crossed just once, at time k. The probability of this is 1−λ, the escape probability for this walk. The ergodic theorem for the crossing counts then gives a cut-edge density of 1−λ.

**Time scale.** A finger of length i has conductances growing like λ^{-depth}, so the return time after entering it is of order λ^{-i}. Entering such a finger and reaching its leaf has probability bounded below. The upper bound follows from Borel–Cantelli on the expected hitting time. The lower bound follows because, among fingers with index in ((1−ε)n, n), at least one is entered with probability 1−e^{-cεn}. Together these give log T_n / n → log(1/λ) almost surely, where T_n is the hitting time of level n.

**Combining.** The furthest level reached by time N satisfies n(N) ~ log N / log(1/λ). Hence M(N) ~ (1−λ) n(N) ~ (1−λ) log N / log(1/λ).

The "(1 - lambda)/log(1/lambda, E)" in the final line is just a notation for the natural logarithm, so it agrees with the boxed result.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
